Simulation-based Q3 cutoffs

Source: R/local_dependence.R
RMlocdepQ3cutoff.Rd

Simulates datasets from a Rasch or partial credit model that fits and resembles your data, and computes \(Q_3\) for every item pair in each. Returns percentiles of the maximum minus mean \(Q_3\) for a global cutoff (Christensen et al., 2017) and an interval per pair. Passed to RMlocdepQ3(), the result gives bootstrap p-values corrected across pairs.

Usage

RMlocdepQ3Cutoff(
  data,
  iterations = 400,
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  cutoff_method = "hdci",
  hdci_width = 0.95,
  estimator = c("CML", "MML"),
  dgp = c("resample", "conditional")
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses, items scored from 0. Respondents with no responses are dropped, incomplete ones are kept.

iterations

Integer. Number of simulated datasets. Default 400, the recommended minimum for reproducible Westfall-Young decisions and the number a 95% interval needs to converge (Johansson, 2026). Use 1000 to 2000 for a final analysis.

parallel

Logical. Run the simulations in parallel via mirai when it is installed. Default TRUE.

n_cores

Integer or NULL. Number of parallel workers. When NULL, getOption("mc.cores") is used. If that is unset too, a warning is given and the simulations run sequentially.

verbose

Logical. Show a progress bar. Default FALSE.

seed

Integer or NULL. Random seed for reproducibility. See easyRasch2-reproducibility for what this guarantees and how it interacts with parallel.

cutoff_method

Character. How the interval per pair in pair_cutoffs is computed: "hdci" (default), the highest-density continuous interval from ggdist::hdci() (needs ggdist), or "quantile", the 2.5th to 97.5th percentiles. The global suggested_cutoff is not affected.

hdci_width

Numeric in (0, 1). Width of the interval with cutoff_method = "hdci". Default 0.95 (0.99 before 1.2.0). The interval describes where a fitting pair's \(Q_3\) is expected to fall and is no longer the default decision rule, so the width is chosen to converge at the default number of iterations. Ignored with "quantile".

estimator

Character. "CML" (default, CML item parameters and WLE person locations) or "MML" (mirt). It is stored in the result and used by RMlocdepQ3() and RMlocdepQ3Plot().

dgp

Character. How datasets are simulated. "resample" (default) draws person locations from the WLE estimates with replacement and simulates responses from the model (a marginal null). Each drawn respondent keeps their pattern of missing responses, so the simulated \(Q_3\) of a pair rests on as many respondents as the observed one. "conditional" simulates each respondent's pattern from the model given their observed total score and answered items, with the item parameters fixed (a conditional null). It needs no latent distribution and avoids the over-dispersion of resampled point estimates. The two give different cutoffs. Experimental.

Value

A list with:

results

data.frame with mean, max and diff (maximum minus mean \(Q_3\)), one row per simulated dataset.

pair_results

data.frame with Item1, Item2, Q3 and iteration, one row per item pair and simulated dataset.

pair_cutoffs

data.frame with the interval per pair: Item1, Item2, Q3_low, Q3_high, computed by cutoff_method.

actual_iterations

Number of simulated datasets that could be used.

requested_iterations

The iterations argument.

sample_n

Number of respondents used (those with at least one response).

sample_n_total

Number of respondents in data.

sample_has_na

Logical. Whether data contained missing values.

sample_summary

Summary of the WLE person locations.

item_names

Item names.

max_diff, sd_diff

Maximum and SD of diff.

p95, p99, p995, p999

Percentiles of diff.

suggested_cutoff

The 99th percentile (p99), the global cutoff for RMlocdepQ3().

cutoff_method

"hdci" or "quantile".

hdci_width

The HDCI width (used only with "hdci").

estimator

"CML" or "MML".

dgp

"resample" or "conditional".

Details

The generating model is fitted once, with CML item parameters (psychotools) and WLE person locations. In each iteration a dataset is simulated by dgp, the model is refitted, and \(Q_3\) is computed with estimator. A simulated dataset that cannot be refitted is left out, and RMlocdepQ3() reports how many in its caption.

Parallel processing needs the optional mirai package.

References

Christensen, K. B., Makransky, G., & Horton, M. (2017). Critical values for Yen's \(Q_3\): Identification of local dependence in the Rasch model. Applied Psychological Measurement, 41(3), 178–194. doi:10.1177/0146621616677520

Johansson, M. (2026). Simulation-based cutoffs for conditional item fit in Rasch models: Iterations, multiplicity correction, and decision stability. PsyArXiv. doi:10.31234/osf.io/7pqz4_v2

See also

RMlocdepQ3() for the tables, RMlocdepQ3Plot() for the plots.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("ggdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(42)
  sim_data <- as.data.frame(
    matrix(sample(0:1, 200 * 10, replace = TRUE), nrow = 200, ncol = 10)
  )
  colnames(sim_data) <- paste0("Item", 1:10)

  # Few iterations for a fast example. Use 1000 or more in real analyses.
  cutoff_res <- RMlocdepQ3Cutoff(sim_data, iterations = 50, parallel = FALSE,
                                 seed = 42)
  cutoff_res$suggested_cutoff  # 99th percentile

  # Use the cutoff in RMlocdepQ3()
  RMlocdepQ3(sim_data, cutoff = cutoff_res$suggested_cutoff)
}
